name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Senegalese Man

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign woman who marries a Senegalese man acquires Senegalese nationality automatically at the time the marriage is celebrated or recognized (Code de la nationalité, Article 7). The government has 1 year to oppose the acquisition by decree. A woman whose own personal law lets her retain her original nationality may decline Senegalese citizenship before the marriage. No equivalent automatic provision exists for a foreign man marrying a Senegalese woman -- he must pursue ordinary naturalization instead, though at a reduced 5-year residency threshold instead of the standard 10 years (see sn_citizenship_naturalisation.json).

sources.title: ecoi.net, hosting an Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) research response on Senegal's citizenship law -- Article 7: automatic citizenship for a foreign wife of a Senegalese man upon marriage, subject to a 1-year government opposition window; no equivalent provision for a foreign husband of a Senegalese woman

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Senegal). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 sourcing limitation as sn_citizenship_by_descent.json; Senegal's own government legal-text sources were not fetchable in this build. GENDERED FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH THE PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY THIS SESSION: automatic marriage-based citizenship exists only for a foreign wife of a Senegalese man. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE PARTIAL MITIGATION, WORTH NOTING RATHER THAN TREATING THIS AS A PURE ONE-SIDED GAP: unlike several other countries built this session where a foreign husband of a citizen woman gets NOTHING marriage-related at all, Senegal's naturalization statute explicitly reduces the standard 10-year residency requirement to 5 years for applicants married to a Senegalese woman -- still a full naturalization application (government decree, no automatic right), but a real, sourced, reduced-threshold accommodation rather than a complete absence of any marriage-linked provision. dual_citizenship_allowed set false here specifically because this is citizenship 'acquired by a decision of the government' (via the 1-year non-opposition mechanism), which the law's Article 16b makes 'incompatible with any other allegiance' -- contrast this with descent-based citizenship in sn_citizenship_by_descent.json, where dual citizenship is allowed pending an 18-25 optional-acquisition choice.
